requirements_summary:
Workload: agent-assist chat in their helpdesk UI (draft responses + conversation summary + next-step suggestions), plus light RAG (rerank + short synth). High repetition across tickets (templates/macros) so they expect prefix caching to materially reduce prefill cost.

Latency/throughput targets:
- p95 end-to-end: <= 900ms for short drafts (<= 250 output tokens), <= 1.5s for summaries (<= 400 output tokens)
- Peak: ~1,200 req/min during business hours; strong diurnal pattern; bursty on incident days

Cost targets (explicit):
- 'We need <$0.007 per ticket for AI, all-in' (their current baseline with another provider is ~2x this)
- Wants per-route token breakdown and cache impact to be visible for internal chargeback

Model preferences:
- Open to curated open models; wants ability to pin model versions and avoid regressions
- Needs safe fallback strategy during capacity events (same route; slightly smaller model acceptable)

Caching expectations + dashboard asks (main theme):
- Must be able to see prefix cache hit-rate and KV cache reuse effectiveness broken down by route + model + region
- Wants 'miss reasons' (TTL expired, version mismatch, policy disabled, capacity) to explain hit-rate drops
- Wants eviction/pressure indicators and a 'wasted prefill' view to detect spend that doesn't convert to reuse
- Wants prompt-length buckets / token histograms without leaking prompt text (privacy constraint)

Security/compliance:
- SOC 2 required (procurement)
- SSO/SAML for Console access; audit logs + retention controls
- Prefers VPC deployment; data residency: US-only for initial rollout
notes:
Account context:
- Aurora Support builds a mid-market helpdesk + agent console (chat + ticketing). Evaluating Redwood for an embedded 'agent copilot'.

What they care about (verbatim-ish):
- 'Caching is the only way this pencils out for us. We need to prove it with dashboards, not guesses.'
- 'If hit-rate drops after a model update, we need to know whether it’s real or telemetry.'

Workload details (current shape):
- Multi-turn chat per ticket; streaming responses in UI
- Prompts include a stable system prefix + macro templates + retrieved snippets
- Expect high prefix reuse across agents and across similar ticket categories

Key evaluation criteria:
- Cache telemetry: prefix hit-rate, KV reuse, eviction pressure, wasted prefill; low cardinality but sliceable by route/model/region
- Operational readiness: alerting guidance for hit-rate regressions; runbook-level clarity
- Cost predictability: per-route $ impact of caching; recommendation-style levers (canonicalization, TTL, routing locality, enable/disable cache per route)

Deployment direction:
- Leaning Dedicated in VPC for predictable latency and isolation; Hosted OK for initial POC if telemetry is representative

Risks / watch-outs:
- They stream; asked specifically how streaming retries and partial reuse are counted (don’t want inflated hit-rate)
- Concerned about prompt privacy: no raw prompts in logs; ok with hashing/bucketing

Internal owners/notes:
- SE (Chloe) to provide a one-pager mapping: 'their questions' -> 'our cache metrics/dashboards'
- Need to confirm what portion of cache dashboards will be customer-visible during POC vs internal report from Telemetry team

Next steps:
- Provide Dedicated (VPC) sizing estimate + POC plan including cache instrumentation validation checklist
- Share sample dashboard screenshots/panels: hit-rate trend, miss reasons, eviction pressure, wasted prefill
- Start security pre-check (SSO/audit logs/retention) in parallel with POC kickoff
